subject: Switchboard: validation of sizing matrix + monitored cutover window
messages:
From: Aaron Patel <aaron@helixai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@helixai.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated: request to validate sizing and pick monitored switch window

Hi Olga,

We are getting close to the commitment for Dedicated capacity (great work getting the PO routed). Before we lock in sizing, the infra team asked for a concrete validation pass against our production traffic and a one-hour monitored switch window during the migration. Two asks: 

1) Can Redwood run a sizing validation using our last 7 days of traffic profile (we can provide logs/p99 latency targets & token distributions)?
2) Propose 2 candidate switch windows in our PST-friendly hours next week for a monitored cutover with rollback controls.

Constraints:
- We need 99th latency < 350ms for single-turn gen workloads (seq len ~512 typical).
- Volume: sustained 200 qps, spikes to 350 qps for ~5–10 minutes several times per day.

I attached the capacity spreadsheet we started; it has the traffic histogram and a current estimate of units. Let me know if you need a live session with our infra folks.

Thanks,
Aaron Patel
Head of Infrastructure
HelixAI

Attachment: helix_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 54KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Patel <aaron@helixai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated: request to validate sizing and pick monitored switch window

Aaron —

Thanks for the level setting and the sheet. We pulled the histogram into our sizing engine and ran a validation pass with a synthetic traffic replay that matches the 7-day profile. High-level findings below; attached is a short playbook PDF with the run notes.

Quick findings:
- Recommended starting fleet: 24 vGPUs (A100-equivalent) in a dedicated pool, configured with medium batching and KV-cache warmed for common prefixes.
- Expected steady-state token cost delta vs hosted: -18% (efficiency wins) with comparable p99 to hosted for the target sequences.
- Under spike (350 qps), the fleet sustains target p99 with short-lived queueing; recommend a conservative burst headroom of 20% (i.e., ability to scale to 29 vGPUs) during the first 48 hours.

Switch windows we can support (PST):
- Option A: Tue 2026-11-30 02:00–03:00 PST (overnight low-traffic window)
- Option B: Wed 2026-12-01 05:00–06:00 PST (early morning with infra team overlap)

Monitored cutover plan (brief):
- 00:00–01:00: Final traffic freeze readouts and KV-warm step (pre-cutover rehearsal).
- 01:00–01:20: Traffic mirror into Dedicated using 10% shadowing.
- 01:20–01:40: Canary route 25% traffic to Dedicated (A/B), health checks and latency gates.
- 01:40–02:00: If gates pass, ramp to 100% over 10 minutes; if not, rollback to hosted.

Pre-reqs we need from HelixAI:
- A sanitized 24-hour log dump from the most recent high-traffic day (we used 7-day already but want a raw day for final validation).
- Confirmation of any traffic shaping or tokenization differences (we noticed a custom token preprocessor in your pipeline).

I've attached the cutover playbook draft: redwood_cutover_playbook_draft.pdf (contains the runbook and rollback checklist).

If this looks good, can we lock Option A as the primary and Option B as backup? I propose a 30-min sync tomorrow so our infra engineers and yours can walk the validation steps.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: redwood_cutover_playbook_draft.pdf (12 pages)

From: Aaron Patel <aaron@helixai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@helixai.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 02:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated: request to validate sizing and pick monitored switch window

Olga,

Appreciate the thorough pass and the draft. Two quick questions from our SRE lead: 
1) The spreadsheet shows medium batching — can you share the expected median token latency at medium vs low batching (we need the numbers for our SLA docs)?
2) If we enable the 20% burst headroom, how quickly can Redwood autoscale from 24 -> 29 vGPUs (ballpark time in seconds/minutes) and what monitoring hooks do you expose for an automated rollback?

We can confirm Option A if those answers look good. We can also do the 30-min sync at 10:00 PST today.

Thanks,
Aaron

On a side note: your note about our tokenizer is correct — we run a small preprocessor that merges line breaks for certain payload types. We'll attach a sanitized sample in the sync.

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Patel <aaron@helixai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated: request to validate sizing and pick monitored switch window

Aaron —

Answers inline: 
- Median token latency: medium batching — ~42ms per token median (end-to-end RPC + execution path measured in our replay). Low batching — ~28ms median, but cost per token increases ~9%. We'll add these numbers into the SLA artifact in Drive.
- Autoscale reaction: our control plane can spin the extra vGPUs and attach them to the pool within ~6–9 minutes (typical path) when cold provisioning is required; if we have pre-warmed spare nodes in the region the path can be <90s. We expose a /v1/health and per-route metrics stream (Prometheus + webhook) and a /v1/rollout endpoint used by customers to trigger automated rollback if latency gates exceed thresholds.

We've confirmed Option A (Tue 2026-11-30 02:00–03:00 PST) as primary. Karthik, Marissa — please confirm availability for the 30-min sync today at 10:00 PST and that the engineering runbook in the Drive link is finalized for the rehearsal.

Thanks —
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.com
